title: The Personal Auto Policy
summary: The 2018 ISO Personal Auto Policy part by part: liability, med pay, uninsured motorists, damage to your auto, duties, and key endorsements.
objectives: Name the six parts of the Personal Auto Policy in order
Recall Part A insureds, supplementary payments and key exclusions
Sort collision from other than collision, plus Michigan's collision options
Match the main endorsements, including Michigan's, to what they do

scenes.title: The Personal Auto Policy
scenes.subtitle: The 2018 ISO form, Parts A through F, and the endorsements that change it

beats.text: Let's walk through the Personal Auto Policy. Its dollar amounts and time limits come from the 2018 edition.
beats.say: Let's walk through the Personal Auto Policy. Its dollar amounts and time limits come from the twenty eighteen edition.

scenes.title: Six parts, in order
scenes.hook: Let Me Use Dad's Dodge, Gramps? - Liability, Medical payments, Uninsured motorists, Damage to your auto, Duties after an accident, General provisions.
items: Part A Liability, Part B Medical Payments
Part C Uninsured Motorists, Part D Damage to Your Auto
Part E Duties After an Accident or Loss, Part F General Provisions
The base form has no PIP or PPI part

beats.text: The policy has six parts, A through F. Let Me Use Dad's Dodge, Gramps? Liability, Medical payments, Uninsured motorists, Damage to your auto, Duties after an accident, General provisions.
beats.say: The policy has six parts, A through F. Let Me Use Dad's Dodge, Gramps? Liability, Medical payments, Uninsured motorists, Damage to your auto, Duties after an accident, General provisions.

beats.text: Notice what's missing: the base form has no PIP or PPI. In Michigan, endorsements add them.
beats.say: Notice what's missing: the base form has no P I P or P P I. In Michigan, endorsements add them.

scenes.title: Part A: Liability
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A: Insuring Agreement A-B; Supplementary Payments

items.label: Insureds
items.detail: You or a family member in any auto; anyone using your covered auto

items.label: Defense costs: on top of the limit
items.detail: Duty to defend ends when the limit is used up

items.label: Bail bonds: up to $250
items.detail: 2018 edition; paid in addition to the limit

items.label: Lost earnings: up to $250 a day
items.detail: For hearings or trials at the insurer's request

beats.text: Part A pays bodily injury and property damage you're legally responsible for. Insureds include you or a family member in any auto, and anyone using your covered auto.
beats.say: Part A pays bodily injury and property damage you're legally responsible for. Insureds include you or a family member in any auto, and anyone using your covered auto.

beats.text: Defense costs are paid in addition to the limit. The duty to defend ends when the limit is used up.
beats.say: Defense costs are paid in addition to the limit. The duty to defend ends when the limit is used up.

beats.text: Supplementary payments are also on top of the limit: up to $250 for bail bonds, and up to $250 a day in lost earnings to attend hearings or trials at the insurer's request.
beats.say: Supplementary payments are also on top of the limit: up to two hundred fifty dollars for bail bonds, and up to two hundred fifty dollars a day in lost earnings to attend hearings or trials at the insurer's request.

scenes.title: Part A exclusions to know
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part A, Exclusions A.5, B.1-B.2

items.label: Public or livery use
items.detail: Includes time logged into a ride-share app as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools are not excluded

items.label: Regular-use vehicles
items.detail: Vehicles furnished or available for your regular use

items.label: Fewer than 4 wheels, or built for off-road
items.detail: With exceptions, such as trailers and non-owned golf carts

beats.text: Three exclusions matter. First, public or livery use, including time logged into a ride-share app as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer use are not excluded.
beats.say: Three exclusions matter. First, public or livery use, including time logged into a ride-share app as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer use are not excluded.

beats.text: Second, vehicles furnished or available for your regular use. Third, vehicles with fewer than 4 wheels or built mainly for off-road use. Endorsements can remove these two for the right vehicles.
beats.say: Second, vehicles furnished or available for your regular use. Third, vehicles with fewer than four wheels or built mainly for off-road use. Endorsements can remove these two for the right vehicles.

scenes.q: Under Part A of the 2018 Personal Auto Policy, the public or livery conveyance exclusion applies to:
choices: Delivering meals to seniors as a volunteer
Time logged into a ride-share app as a driver
scenes.why: The 2018 PAP's livery exclusion expressly includes time logged into a transportation network platform as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer or charitable use are excepted.

beats.text: Quick check. Under the 2018 policy, which activity falls under the public or livery conveyance exclusion? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. Under the twenty eighteen policy, which activity falls under the public or livery conveyance exclusion? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The answer is time logged into a ride-share app as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer use are not excluded.
reveal.say: The answer is time logged into a ride-share app as a driver. Share-the-expense car pools and volunteer use are not excluded.

scenes.title: Part B and Part C
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part B A-B; Part C A, C; DIFS auto FAQ; Rory v Continental (2005)

columns.name: Part B: Medical Payments
points: Services within 3 years of the accident
You and family members, even as pedestrians

columns.name: Part C: Uninsured Motorists
points: Bodily injury an uninsured driver owes you
Michigan: listed by DIFS as optional

scenes.tell: Part B: your medical bills, for services within 3 years. Part C: the injury damages an uninsured driver owes you.

beats.text: Part B, medical payments, pays medical and funeral expenses for services within 3 years of the accident. It covers you and family members, even as pedestrians, and anyone in your covered auto.
beats.say: Part B, medical payments, pays medical and funeral expenses for services within three years of the accident. It covers you and family members, even as pedestrians, and anyone in your covered auto.

beats.text: Part C, uninsured motorists, pays bodily injury damages an uninsured driver owes you. Hit-and-runs and insolvent insurers count. Government-owned vehicles don't.
beats.say: Part C, uninsured motorists, pays bodily injury damages an uninsured driver owes you. Hit-and-runs and insolvent insurers count. Government-owned vehicles don't.

beats.text: In Michigan, DIFS lists UM and UIM as optional coverages, and the Michigan Supreme Court treats UM as optional.
beats.say: In Michigan, D I F S lists U M and U I M as optional coverages, and the Michigan Supreme Court treats U M as optional.

scenes.title: Part D: collision or other than collision?
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D, Insuring Agreement B
scenes.hook: Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer (or a bird) is Other Than Collision. Hitting a tree, another car, or rolling over is Collision.
items: Collision: upset of the auto, or impact with a vehicle or object
Other than collision: fire, theft, windstorm, hail, flood, vandalism, falling objects
Hitting a bird or animal: other than collision
Glass broken in a collision: collision, at your option

beats.text: Part D covers your own auto. Collision is the upset of your auto, or its impact with another vehicle or object.
beats.say: Part D covers your own auto. Collision is the upset of your auto, or its impact with another vehicle or object.

beats.text: Other than collision covers perils like fire, theft, windstorm, hail, flood, vandalism and falling objects.
beats.say: Other than collision covers perils like fire, theft, windstorm, hail, flood, vandalism and falling objects.

beats.text: And Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer is other than collision. Swerve and hit a tree instead? Collision.
beats.say: And Bambi is not a collision: hitting a deer is other than collision. Swerve and hit a tree instead? Collision.

beats.text: Glass broken in a collision may be treated as collision, at your option.
beats.say: Glass broken in a collision may be treated as collision, at your option.

scenes.title: Michigan collision options

columns.name: Limited
points: Pays only if not substantially at fault

columns.name: Broad form
points: Deductible waived if not substantially at fault

columns.name: Standard
points: You pay the deductible either way

scenes.tell: Substantially at fault means more than 50% of the cause.

beats.text: In Michigan, insurers must offer limited and broad form collision at a first private passenger application. Limited has no deductible, but pays only if the driver was not substantially at fault.
beats.say: In Michigan, insurers must offer limited and broad form collision at a first private passenger application. Limited has no deductible, but pays only if the driver was not substantially at fault.

beats.text: Broad form pays regardless of fault, and waives the deductible if the driver was not substantially at fault. Standard collision may also be offered: you pay the deductible either way.
beats.say: Broad form pays regardless of fault, and waives the deductible if the driver was not substantially at fault. Standard collision may also be offered: you pay the deductible either way.

beats.text: Substantially at fault means more than 50% of the cause.
beats.say: Substantially at fault means more than fifty percent of the cause.

scenes.title: Sam's new car
scenes.story: Sam buys a second car on Monday. No auto on his policy has collision coverage. On Wednesday, before calling his insurer, he backs the new car into a pole. He calls on Thursday to ask for collision.

items.label: Any declared auto with collision?
items.detail: No, so Sam had 4 days to ask, not 14

items.label: Did he ask in time?
items.detail: Yes, within 4 days, so coverage began when he became the owner

scenes.answer: Covered, with a $500 deductible. Had he asked late, coverage would begin only when he asked.

beats.text: Sam buys a second car Monday. No auto on his policy has collision. Wednesday, before calling his insurer, he backs into a pole. Thursday, he asks for collision. Is he covered?
beats.say: Sam buys a second car Monday. No auto on his policy has collision. Wednesday, before calling his insurer, he backs into a pole. Thursday, he asks for collision. Is he covered?

beats.text: If a declared auto had collision, he'd have 14 days to ask. With none, the window is 4 days. Sam asked within 4 days.
beats.say: If a declared auto had collision, he'd have fourteen days to ask. With none, the window is four days. Sam asked within four days.

beats.text: So he's covered from the day he became the owner, but a deductible of $500 applies to a loss before he asked.
beats.say: So he's covered from the day he became the owner, but a deductible of five hundred dollars applies to a loss before he asked.

scenes.title: Transportation expenses (2018 edition)
scenes.src: ISO PP 00 01 09 18, Part D, Transportation Expenses

items.label: Other losses: car out of use more than

beats.text: Part D also pays transportation expenses with no deductible: up to $30 a day, to $900. Thirty times thirty is nine hundred.
beats.say: Part D also pays transportation expenses with no deductible: up to thirty dollars a day, to nine hundred dollars. Thirty times thirty is nine hundred.

beats.text: After a total theft, payment starts 48 hours after the theft. For other losses, the car must be out of use more than 24 hours.
beats.say: After a total theft, payment starts forty-eight hours after the theft. For other losses, the car must be out of use more than twenty-four hours.

scenes.title: Part E: duties after an accident or loss

items.label: Hit-and-run UM claim: tell police promptly

beats.text: Part E lists your duties: prompt notice, cooperation, sending legal papers, exams, records and proof of loss. For a hit-and-run uninsured motorists claim, promptly notify the police.
beats.say: Part E lists your duties: prompt notice, cooperation, sending legal papers, exams, records and proof of loss. For a hit-and-run uninsured motorists claim, promptly notify the police.

beats.text: The insurer has no duty to provide coverage if your failure to comply is prejudicial to it.
beats.say: The insurer has no duty to provide coverage if your failure to comply is prejudicial to it.

scenes.title: Endorsements, including Michigan's
scenes.src: PP 03 23 per FC&S summary (form text not read); PP 03 06 01 05; DIFS Bulletin 96-02; MCL 500.3107, 3109(3), 3121

items.label: Miscellaneous Type Vehicle
items.detail: Motor homes, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, golf carts. Snowmobiles: separate form

items.label: Extended Non-Owned
items.detail: Removes the regular-use exclusion, for example a car an employer furnishes

items.label: Michigan: DIFS Bulletin 96-02
items.detail: Non-owner endorsements give residual liability only, to named person and spouse

items.label: Michigan PIP and PPI endorsements
items.detail: Add the no-fault benefits. A PIP deductible applies only to your household

beats.text: Now endorsements. Miscellaneous Type Vehicle typically covers motor homes, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, dune buggies and golf carts. Snowmobiles use a separate endorsement.
beats.say: Now endorsements. Miscellaneous Type Vehicle typically covers motor homes, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, dune buggies and golf carts. Snowmobiles use a separate endorsement.

beats.text: Extended Non-Owned removes the regular-use exclusion for liability, and med pay if bought. It fits someone who regularly drives an employer's car.
beats.say: Extended Non-Owned removes the regular-use exclusion for liability, and med pay if bought. It fits someone who regularly drives an employer's car.

beats.text: But in Michigan, a DIFS bulletin says named non-owner and extended non-owned endorsements give residual liability only, for the named person and spouse. No PIP, no PPI, no physical damage.
beats.say: But in Michigan, a D I F S bulletin says named non-owner and extended non-owned endorsements give residual liability only, for the named person and spouse. No P I P, no P P I, no physical damage.

beats.text: Michigan PIP and PPI endorsements add the no-fault benefits. A PIP deductible applies only to the named insured, spouse and resident relatives.
beats.say: Michigan P I P and P P I endorsements add the no-fault benefits. A P I P deductible applies only to the named insured, spouse and resident relatives.

scenes.q: According to DIFS, a named non-owner or extended non-owned endorsement on a Michigan no-fault policy provides:
choices: PIP, PPI and residual liability for the whole household
Residual liability only, for the named person and spouse
scenes.why: DIFS Bulletin 96-02: these endorsements provide only residual liability, only for the named person and spouse. They give no PIP, PPI or physical damage, and don't meet no-fault requirements.

beats.text: Your turn. According to DIFS, what do these Michigan non-owner endorsements provide? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. According to D I F S, what do these Michigan non-owner endorsements provide? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The answer is residual liability only, for the named person and spouse. That's why such an endorsement doesn't meet Michigan's no-fault requirements.
reveal.say: The answer is residual liability only, for the named person and spouse. That's why such an endorsement doesn't meet Michigan's no-fault requirements.

items: Parts A to F: Let Me Use Dad's Dodge, Gramps?
Part A (2018): defense plus $250 bail and $250 a day, on top of limits
Deer: other than collision. Rollover or hitting a tree: collision
New car (2018): 14 days to ask; 4 if no declared auto has it
Michigan non-owner endorsements: residual liability only
